decisions.title: Review the first accountable Angular release
decisions.recommendation: Review publication-set-c7ad466d0f6a012f as the first founder-controlled Firebase release candidate.
decisions.decisionQuestion: Does this exact content set represent the site you want readers to see first?
decisions.rationale: The research and release machinery cannot create traffic, trust, or revenue while the modern reviewed site remains only a local candidate.
evidence: 10 publication-ready articles are in the candidate set.
10 independent QA receipts are hash-bound to those articles.
60 reviewed social drafts are prepared for later distribution.
No managed Firebase content-release receipt is durably recorded in Git yet.
decisions.unlocks: A protected exact-SHA preview and founder-reviewed Firebase release establish the owned destination for every later growth and affiliate action.
decisions.tradeoff: The first release creates a public baseline and monitoring responsibility, while affiliate links and social publishing remain separately disabled.
decisions.guardrail: Commit and review the exact candidate first; the workflow must still clone live, expose the preview, require founder approval, smoke production, and mint a manifest-bound receipt.

decisions.title: Configure the first aggregate measurement source
decisions.recommendation: Start with the exact canonical URL-prefix property and read-only page aggregates before adding broader analytics.
decisions.decisionQuestion: Do you approve configuring the low-data first measurement path for organic discovery?
decisions.rationale: Traffic, conversions, and revenue are currently unknown. Measurement must exist before the team can distinguish useful growth work from activity.
evidence: 0 complete aggregate measurement snapshots are available.
3 experiments are proposed but cannot run without a baseline.
Founder verifies the site property and approves aggregate Search Console export access.
decisions.unlocks: A complete baseline lets the growth lead rank articles by real search demand and propose experiments with measurable stop conditions.
decisions.tradeoff: Even aggregate measurement adds account, access, and review work, but starting with search avoids unnecessary behavioral tracking.
decisions.guardrail: Use the exact URL-prefix property, read-only OAuth scope, page filters only, finalized seven-day windows, no raw queries, no identifiers, and no experiment activation from partial data.

decisions.title: Decide whether Pinterest becomes the first owned distribution channel
decisions.recommendation: Configure pinterest as the first bounded channel only after the official account, API, rights, cadence, and reporting posture are approved.
decisions.decisionQuestion: Do you want to establish the official Pinterest operating envelope for the prepared launch queue?
decisions.rationale: The team has reusable decision-first creative, but drafts cannot drive traffic until one official channel has a founder-approved and measurable publishing boundary.
evidence: 1 original creative candidate is locally verified.
decisions.unlocks: A configured channel allows byte-level media approval and content approval; active status later enables only protected per-post official-API publishing.
decisions.tradeoff: An owned social account creates moderation, policy, rights, and cadence obligations before it produces measurable traffic.
decisions.guardrail: Do not browser-post or store credentials in Git. Keep every post separately approved and require an official external post ID before calling it published.

decisions.title: Choose a narrow affiliate onboarding pilot
decisions.recommendation: Review Bookshop.org US media affiliate first because it has the smallest current eligible-article footprint.
decisions.decisionQuestion: Is this program worth the external account, terms, disclosure, and reporting burden?
decisions.rationale: A narrow pilot can test operational fit with less commission pressure than enabling the broadest catalog before traffic and conversion evidence exist.
evidence: 2 affiliate programs await founder review and 0 await external activation evidence.
0 programs and 0 tracked links are enabled.
Bookshop.org US media affiliate currently maps to 1 publication-ready article.
decisions.unlocks: Founder approval permits external onboarding review; a later audited activation can allow validated paid links without changing editorial rank.
decisions.tradeoff: Enrollment and reporting add compliance work, while a narrow program covers fewer products and cannot monetize every companion in a pair.
decisions.guardrail: Approval does not accept terms, create an account, enable links, invent a tracking identity, or change product ranking.

programs.name: Bookshop.org US media affiliate
programs.editorialFit: A focused first candidate for book anchors in evidence-backed pairs, with a storefront model that can support independent bookstores.
limitations: It does not replace a general merchant program for non-book companions, so pair recommendations must remain independently useful with ordinary links.
Attribution, compensation, onboarding, disclosure, and product availability must be rechecked against current terms before activation.
programs.nextGate: Lucas decides whether this mission-aligned book program is worth external enrollment; approval records the decision but does not accept terms or enable links.

programs.name: Amazon Associates US
programs.editorialFit: A broad-catalog candidate that could cover books, games, golf accessories, and practical gifts without changing the editorial ranking.
limitations: The agreement and incorporated program policies can change, so every link format, registered site, disclosure, and content-use rule needs a fresh activation review.
A broad catalog can create commission bias; the recommendation order and ordinary manufacturer alternatives must remain unchanged when paid tracking is removed.
programs.nextGate: Lucas reviews the current agreement and operating burden before any external signup; no Special Link or disclosure is generated until the account is explicitly activated.
